records.text: Pam Bondi disbanded the Foreign Influence Task Force on her first day, eliminating the DOJ office responsible for enforcing FARA.
records.speaker: Ian Carroll

appearances.snippet: Pam Bondi, on her first day, disbands the Foreign Influence Task Force, the very DOJ office responsible for enforcing FARA, the Foreign Agents Registration Act.

verification.notes: Attorney General Bondi’s February 5, 2025 memorandum did disband the Foreign Influence Task Force. But it did not eliminate the FARA Unit: the same memo directed the Counterintelligence and Export Control Section, including the FARA Unit, to focus on civil enforcement, regulatory initiatives, and public guidance. The statement is correct on disbandment but wrong that the DOJ office responsible for FARA was eliminated.

records.text: The change limits DOJ prosecutors from criminally charging public-relations and policy-advocacy work for foreign businesses and nonprofits.
records.speaker: Ian Carroll

appearances.snippet: The change specifically limits DOJ prosecutors from criminally charging those involved in public relations work and policy advocacy on behalf of foreign businesses and nonprofits.

verification.notes: The DOJ memo limits FARA and section 951 criminal charges to alleged conduct resembling traditional espionage by foreign government actors and shifts the FARA Unit toward civil enforcement. That broadly reduces criminal exposure for ordinary advocacy and public-relations work, but the memo does not categorically immunize all PR or policy advocacy for foreign businesses and nonprofits.
